rationales.1: Each card shows price, stock state, sow window, and difficulty in fixed positions, and the shelf sections plus month dropdown make season filtering simple and predictable.
rationales.2: Price and stock sit where convention expects them and the product buy box is a textbook quantity-plus-add pattern with the delivery note beside it. The only oddity is that a visible view button appears on just one card.
rationales.3: Out of stock is plainly marked, the null-price packet honestly says price on request, the estimated germination is flagged inline, and the UK-only banner appears before any purchase intent forms.
rationales.4: Generous card type, a large add-to-basket target, and no hover-dependent information hold up at both widths, and mobile keeps full content in a single readable column.
rationales.5: The packet-illustration cards, limited cream-rust-green palette, and consistent spacing carry across catalog and product page as one system, with only minor busyness inside the cards.
rationales.6: The sowing table, difficulty line, potting-shed note, and companion cards with price and stock let a first-time gardener decide entirely on the page.
rationales.7: The seed rack by the shop door is a one-sentence idea a two-person shop could truthfully own, and the shelf sections, packet art, and copy all reinforce it.
rationales.8: The novelty lives in the shelf metaphor and botanical packet art while every money-path mechanic stays strictly conventional.
rationales.9: Lines like fruits indoors through winter on a bright sill and kept in one family since 1928 are warm and specific, though the voice thins outside the descriptions.
rationales.10: Season shelves plus the month filter answer what can I sow now immediately, low-stock counts are surfaced, and the two surfaces share one visual language.
